item.title: French prime minister says government not indifferent to students' concerns in TV address
item.description: In a televised address from his official residence the French prime minister acknowledges young people anger 'doesn't come from nowhere' and promises a plan to respond to the crisis

item.title: Judo: Grigalashvili claims fourth world title as Kaju reigns again
item.description: Haruka Kaju extended her unbeaten World Judo Tour run to 40 contests, defending her -63kg world title against Kerem Primo. At -81kg, Tato Grigalashvili defeated home favourite Zelim Tckaev to claim his fourth world title and return to the top of the podium.

item.title: Southern right whales return to South Africa, drawing crowds to the coast
item.description: Southern right whales return to Hermanus, South Africa, drawing crowds to the cliffs and whale festival as mothers nurse newborn calves in Walker Bay.

item.title: Maricarmen, symbol of Spain's housing protests, dies
item.description: The 87-year-old woman had withstood four eviction attempts in the past decade. In a final message from her hospital bed, she urged protesters: "Fight!"

item.title: Unexpected beach guest: Elephant seal draws crowds in Rio
item.description: A southern elephant seal surprised Rio’s Copacabana beachgoers, drawing crowds, photos and social media buzz as officials set up barriers to protect it.

item.title: Poland’s economic rise - Can it last? The Ring in Warsaw
item.description: The Ring travels to the Polish capital for a political discussion on the country’s economic transformation and the challenges ahead.

item.title: Trump mocks Sheinbaum over Gulf of Mexico and imitates her alleged reaction: 'No, no, please'
item.description: The US president says the Mexican leader rang him to urge him not to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Trump justified the change with coastal data that available figures do not support.

item.title: Rubio in Athens urges Europe to shoulder more of its defence burden
item.description: The US secretary of state held talks on energy, military cooperation and regional security, pointing to Greece as an example of higher defence spending. The agenda also included LNG, F-35s, the Eastern Mediterranean and the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Knife attack at Polish school: in Ostroleka a student injures seven, two are in critical condition
item.description: On Wednesday morning at a vocational school in Ostrołęka in Northern Poland, a 19-year-old pupil attacked classmates and teachers with a sharp tool, injuring seven people, two of whom are in a serious condition, police said.

item.title: Fantasy worlds come to life on nails at London nail art competition
item.description: Nailympia London showcased fantasy nail art inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk, as global artists raced to create miniature worlds on nails.

item.title: Rebranded Jaguar unveils its first electric sportscar: The Type 01EV
item.description: Hailed as the most technologically advanced and powerful Jaguar in the company’s history, it premiered in New York today, targeting a younger, wealthier and mostly American customer base.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 7th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 7th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Milan looks East: Chinese fashion takes centre stage for traditional craftwork
item.description: Brocade carries centuries of Chinese history, woven with patterns that have long held meanings beyond decoration. Now, the traditional craft is finding a new expression on the Milan catwalk, as designers reinterpret the fabric for a contemporary audience.

item.title: Russia dismisses transparency calls amid reports of second Siberia plague case
item.description: Rospotrebnadzor said nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens and saw "no epidemic risk," while the Kremlin called most media reporting "false" and said it had no knowledge of a US demarche formally requesting additional information.

item.title: Deadly drone attacks raise questions over Europe’s Black Sea defences
item.description: The European Union has a plan to safeguard the Black Sea. But days after drones wreaked havoc along Romania and Bulgaria’s coast, sinking commercial vessels and killing two people, questions loom over how Brussels can protect the sea.

item.title: ‘We will certainly look at it’: Trump says he will consider permanent US military base in Lithuania
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he would consider Lithuania’s proposal to permanently host US troops after the Baltic country said it was ready to accommodate a permanent American military presence.

item.title: Residents search belongings after Jerusalem building demolished
item.description: A five-storey building in Jerusalem’s al-Tur was demolished by Israeli authorities over alleged lack of permits, displacing dozens of Palestinian residents.

item.title: MEPs urge tougher action against China as tensions hit ‘critical point’
item.description: The resolution calls China “a decisive enabler” of Russia’s war in Ukraine and says the EU should take action against China’s weaponisation of the rare eath minerals that Europe depends on.

item.title: ‘A worrying decline’: Why penguins are vanishing from this volcanic island 2,000km from humans
item.description: Scientists have blamed human-caused climate change for the decline in chinstrap penguins on the remote Zavodovski Island.

item.title: Exclusive: The Left group wants to halve MEP salaries
item.description: The proposal would slash MEPs’ net monthly salary from around €8,800 to almost €4,400, but opponents have dismissed it as a “populist stunt”.

item.title: EU hopefuls fear new safeguard plans could create second-class members
item.description: EU candidate countries fear safeguards designed to prevent democratic backsliding, like a planned 15-year probation period, could create second-class membership and be used to exert political pressure.

item.title: Menopause drug Lenzetto to return to Spanish pharmacies in November
item.description: Gedeon Richter has told "Euronews" it expects to resume supply of this menopause treatment in Spain from mid-November, but warns global limits may stop it meeting demand in 2027.

item.title: Former BND chief's aide arrested as Germany's biggest spy scandal widens
item.description: Manfred D, former head of cabinet to ex-intelligence chief August Hanning, was taken into custody on charges of aiding and abetting treason. He is accused of obtaining classified BND documents and passing them to Hanning in exchange for payment since 2010.

item.title: Italians and Czechs push Brussels to ease green rules as energy crisis hits industry
item.description: Rome and Prague have joined forces to protect industry ahead of the EU leaders' summit in Brussels next week.

item.title: Iran threatens pre-emptive strikes as US questions who runs Tehran
item.description: Iran's army spokesman said Tehran's forces were prepared to strike first "should circumstances require it," while IRGC officials claimed tighter control of Hormuz, and Washington publicly pondered how much authority Pezeshkian and Araghchi actually wielded.

item.title: Longevity: why do Poles live shorter than Western Europeans?
item.description: Poland still clearly trails Western Europe in life expectancy and years lived in good health. According to Robert Mordaka, a public health specialist, prevention and everyday habits are crucial.

item.title: Europe’s travel and tourism industry to grow 3.1% in 2026, new figures reveal
item.description: The new statistics were released during the opening day of the World Travel & Tourism Council’s global summit in Malta.

item.title: Madrid versus Latin America: Where is housing more affordable?
item.description: Homes cost more per square metre in Madrid than in several major Latin American cities, but lower wages in those cities can make renting even less affordable.

item.title: Iran parliament votes to criminalise interviews with 'hostile' foreign media
item.description: The bill passed 174 to six despite cabinet opposition, carrying penalties of up to two years in prison, fines and flogging for Iranians who speak to outlets designated as hostile by the Intelligence Ministry. The bill has not yet become law and faces Guardian Council review.

item.title: Mercedes global sales fall 6% as electric car sales hit record high
item.description: Mercedes-Benz shares fell after the German carmaker reported a 6% fall in global sales, driven by weakness in China. Sales outside China edged higher, supported by growth in Europe and North America.

item.title: Inside Kazakhstan’s historic rock-hewn mosques now recognised by UNESCO
item.description: Five rock-hewn mosques and associated sacred sites dating from the 12th to the 18th centuries make up Kazakhstan’s newest UNESCO World Heritage property. The complexes preserve centuries of Sufi tradition alongside much older beliefs.

item.title: Judo 2026 World Championships: Koga and Yusifov Strike Gold on Opening Day in Baku
item.description: Wakana Koga claimed her first world title at -48kg, defeating Assunta Scutto in the final. At -60kg, home favourite Ahmad Yusifov came from behind to beat Sherzod Davlatov, sending the Baku crowd into celebration on an unforgettable opening day.

item.title: France suspends police stun grenades at student protests after teenager loses hand
item.description: More than 6,500 people, most of them minors, have been arrested since the movement began and one teenager lost his hand when handling a police grenade.

item.title: Interlaken vs Innsbruck: How Europe’s adventure travel hotspots compare for a winter holiday
item.description: These Alpine adventure destinations offers snow-covered slopes, unique hotels and local delicacies. But between Interlaken and Innsbruck, where should you choose to travel this winter?

item.title: EU agrees to sanction over 1,600 people and entities linked to Russia's war
item.description: The EU will soon add over 1,600 names, including 77 lawmakers who stood for election in the occupied territories of Ukraine, to its Russia sanctions. The decision comes amid an unsettling rise in hybrid attacks.

item.title: Scientists identify ancient Egyptian crocodile whose skull is missing its nose like the Sphinx
item.description: A skull found nearly a century ago has helped Egyptian and European researchers revise part of the crocodile family tree, shedding light on the Mediterranean's prehistoric wildlife and revealing an unexpected connection to the Great Sphinx.

item.title: Laws, pledges or an iron grip? How the EU, US and China are reining in AI
item.description: The US, China and the EU are taking sharply different approaches to regulating artificial intelligence. Here is how the world's biggest economies are tackling the technology, and what is at stake.

item.title: Willem de Kooning returns to the Netherlands for major Rijksmuseum exhibition
item.description: A century after leaving the Netherlands for New York, Willem de Kooning is returning home in a major new exhibition at Amsterdam’s Rijksmuseum.

item.title: One-minute siren sounds in Tel Aviv to mark October 7 anniversary
item.description: A one-minute siren sounded in Tel Aviv as Israelis gathered to mark the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks and remember those killed.

item.title: Finland orders pause on Google AI data centres over environmental concerns
item.description: Google had called the data centres its biggest investment in Europe.

item.title: Tokyo sleep competition offers 2 million yen prize to best sleeper
item.description: A Tokyo sleep competition organised by Koala offered ¥2 million to the best sleeper, highlighting Japan’s long-hours work culture and sleep deprivation.

item.title: Trump to talk plague with Putin as Russia plays down fears of outbreak
item.description: The Kremlin welcomed the offer while Russia's health watchdog shot back that Moscow was "ready to assist the US in tackling infectious disease outbreaks" as the WHO asked Russia for additional information.

item.title: Hungary set to lift veto on Ukraine's EU membership talks
item.description: Hungary dropped its veto on two clusters of Ukraine's EU accession talks on Wednesday. The next phase depends on Kyiv's parliament passing a minority-rights law.

item.title: EU releases €1.24 billion for Ukrainian-made drones and munitions
item.description: The European Union has released €1.24 billion for Ukraine to buy drones, drone interceptors, drone ammunition and munitions manufactured domestically in a bid to push back against Russia's ongoing and escalated air attacks.

item.title: Plague fears in Siberia: How are Irkutsk residents reacting?
item.description: Irkutsk residents react to reports of a suspected pneumonic plague death at a local anti-plague institute, with authorities saying the cause of death remains unconfirmed.

item.title: Kyiv residents take refuge underground during overnight Russian attacks
item.description: Kyiv residents took refuge in metro stations, preparing to sleep underground before a Russian missile and drone attack killed at least eight people.

item.title: French and Japanese scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for what could change how medicines are made
item.description: Two researchers have won this year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work that could change how medicines are made.

item.title: Italy lets diesel tax cut expire as Europe tackles fuel costs
item.description: The Meloni government has neither renewed the diesel tax cut nor launched the replacement scheme it had promised. EU leaders meet on 15–16 October, while European governments pursue different measures to ease fuel costs.

item.title: EU to put energy security at heart of COP31 push for faster green transition
item.description: EU ministers are set to confirm their commitment to the green transition despite soaring energy prices and supply concerns, according to a draft COP31 position seen by Euronews.

item.title: İzmir's centre-left mayor joins Erdoğan's AK Party, shocking Turkish opposition
item.description: Cemil Tugay, who won İzmir for the CHP with a 314,000-vote margin in 2024, received his AK Party badge from Erdoğan in Ankara on Wednesday, ending 27 years of centre-left rule in Turkey's third-largest city.
